q: The marina asks you to spell your yacht's name, KIRA. What do you say?
why: The phonetic alphabet: K Kilo, I India, R Romeo, A Alfa.

q: The marina's reply is drowned out by an engine starting nearby; you understood nothing. What do you send?
why: SAY AGAIN asks for the whole message again; REPEAT is not used for this on the radio.

q: The marina gives you your berth and the code for the shower block. You have understood it all. Which word confirms that?
why: RECEIVED means the message has been heard and understood.

q: You confirm to the marina that your berth is number 9. How do you say the figure?
why: On the radio the figure 9 is spoken "niner" so it is not confused with other words.

q: The marina asks your draft. It is 2.9 m. What do you say?
why: Figures are spoken one by one, with "decimal" for the point and "niner" for 9.

q: You hear: "Aurora, this is Vega Marina, go to pontoon Charlie…" and the rest is lost in noise. What do you send?
why: ALL AFTER asks for everything that followed the word you name.

q: You told the marina: "Berth for one night, catamaran, twelve metres, OVER". They reply: "Aurora, SAY AGAIN ALL BEFORE twelve metres, OVER". What do you repeat?
why: ALL BEFORE asks for everything that came before the word named.

q: The marina cannot catch your yacht's name, Xenia. How do you give it?
a: "Xenia, I SPELL, X-ray Echo November India Alfa"
o: "Xenia, CORRECTION, X-ray Echo November India Alfa"
"Xenia, SAY AGAIN, X-ray Echo November India Alfa"
"Xenia, I SPELL, Xylophone Echo Nancy India Alfa"
why: I SPELL tells the listener the next words are letters of the phonetic alphabet.

q: You have just said "length one four metres", but Aurora is 12 m long. What do you say at once?
why: CORRECTION cancels your last word or phrase; the right version follows.

q: The marina asks for your boat's registration number. It is in the papers below and will take you a couple of minutes to find. Which proword do you use first?
why: WAIT, with the minutes if you can, tells the other station you need a pause.

q: The marina asks: "Aurora, do you need shore power, OVER?" You do. What do you reply?
why: AFFIRMATIVE means yes; RECEIVED only says you heard the question.

q: You hear "Aurora, Aurora, this is …" but the caller's name is lost in noise. How do you answer?
a: "Station calling Aurora, this is Aurora, OVER"
o: "Who is calling Aurora? Identify yourself, OVER"
"All stations, this is Aurora, SAY AGAIN, OVER"
"Aurora, this is Aurora, SAY AGAIN, OUT"
why: STATION CALLING answers a call when you did not catch who made it.

q: You must read out your latitude. How do you say it?
a: "Three seven degrees five two decimal four minutes north"
o: "Thirty-seven degrees fifty-two point four minutes north"
"Three seven degrees fifty-two decimal four minutes north"
"Five two decimal four minutes, three seven degrees north"
why: Positions are read figure by figure: degrees, minutes with "decimal", then north or south.

q: The coastguard asks for your MMSI, 237012340. How do you say it?
a: "Two three seven zero one two three four zero"
o: "Two three seven one two three four"
why: Long numbers are given figure by figure, zeros included.

q: The marina said your berth was "fifteen", and you went to berth 50. How should numbers be given to avoid this?
o: As a word, said twice: "fifteen, fifteen"
why: Saying figures one by one stops "fifteen" and "fifty" being confused.

q: Your crew calls: "Vega Marina, Aurora, OVER". The marina is unsure who is calling whom. What is missing?
a: THIS IS, between the name called and your own name
o: OVER AND OUT, at the very end of the call
I SPELL, before the name of your yacht
RECEIVED, before the name of the marina
why: THIS IS separates the station called from the station calling.

q: The marina's reply reaches you like this. What do you send?
why: WORD AFTER asks for the single word that followed the one you name.

q: The coastguard asks your position. How do you read it out?
a: "Three six degrees two seven decimal niner minutes north, zero two five degrees zero eight decimal three minutes east"
o: "Thirty-six degrees twenty-seven decimal nine north, twenty-five degrees eight decimal three east"
"Three six degrees two seven decimal niner minutes north, two five degrees eight decimal three minutes east"
"Three six degrees two seven decimal niner minutes east, zero two five degrees zero eight decimal three minutes north"
why: Latitude first, then longitude with three figures of degrees; all figures one by one.

q: The marina gives you pontoon B, berth 19. You read it back to confirm. Which is right?
why: Letters in the phonetic alphabet (B = Bravo), figures one by one with "niner".

q: The marina says: "Aurora, berth one five, CORRECTION, berth one six, pontoon Charlie, OVER". Where do you go?
why: CORRECTION cancels what came just before it; the version after it stands.
